dossier.architecture: Fixed-angle shooter and telescoping traversal mechanism with deliberately replaceable collector.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; module detail not established in reviewed excerpt.
subsystems.intake: Early flap/Velcro concept repelled cargo; rubber followed Wilsonville, then an offseason griptape tube. Polycarbonate breakaways and quick assembly replacement protect the core.
subsystems.transfer: Mecanum centering, polycord uptake, ultrasonic capacity feedback and driver haptics.
subsystems.scoring: Fixed heading and fixed elevation; powered back roller controls spin. Team accepted a bounded shooting area around the tarmac.
subsystems.endgame: Four belt-telescoping arms; inner and outer pairs sequence through bars with swing timing. Sub-three-second claim belongs to the Chezy configuration.
subsystems.controls: Driver feedback and repeatable shot locations reduce aiming complexity.

versions: Offseason collector and fast climb shown in Chezy interview; do not assume those timings at early events.
dossier.analysis: A narrower shooting envelope can buy lower mass, easier tuning and a strong endgame. The correct comparison is points per reliable cycle over a realistic route, not adjustable versus fixed in isolation.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2022-2046 · A bounded shooting envelope can be an intentional simplification
context_documents.body:
# 2022-2046: A bounded shooting envelope can be an intentional simplification

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The collector moves from early flap/Velcro contacts through rubber to a later griptape tube. Breakaway members protect the core. A fixed-heading, fixed-elevation launcher uses a powered back roller and accepts a bounded shooting region; the climb uses swing to reach traversal.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The source explicitly reports early contacts repelling cargo and later material experiments. The retained account treats the limited shooting area as an accepted design constraint.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Range is not free capability. A simpler scorer can be effective if its reachable positions, acquisition routes and defended access remain adequate. Offseason material changes must not be back-projected onto Worlds.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test access to the preferred scoring area under defense and compare collector materials with consistent cargo and approach speed.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers 2046 Bear Metal | Rapid React
source_reviews.review_basis: Read timestamped English transcript of the team interview at Chezy Champs.
facts: The team reports three pickup surface states, unequal-thickness sacrificial polycarbonate pieces and a complete spare collector.
Ultrasonic detection advances the superstructure a controlled distance and triggers driver vibration. Printed rollers center the poly belts.
Fixed angle reduces mass. Continuous belt telescopes and an inner/outer arm sequence use swing to reach traversal.
limitations: The climb speed is a postseason team claim, with no timing distribution or visual audit.

source_reviews.title: 2046 Robot — Rapid React
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team replies in indexed Chief Delphi thread.
facts: The March intake used printed hubs and urethane belting strips. The fixed hood was set for upper-hub shots from beyond eight feet and could use the launchpad.
limitations: Early material details and the stated range boundary apply to the published Wilsonville-era configuration.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Amelia Bearhart uses a swerve base to position a fixed-heading, fixed-angle upper-hub shooter. Cargo collection and staging are designed around quick recovery after contact and clear feedback about the two-piece load. Four belt-driven telescoping arms give endgame separate contact sets, so the shooter does not have to carry a rung hook.
source_review.piece_flow: At Chezy, a griptape-covered tube and mecanum contacts gather floor cargo and converge it directly into the superstructure. The first cargo advances a controlled distance. On detection of another ball, the existing ball is moved farther up to make room. Controller vibration marks acquisition and the count caps at two. Printed rollers track poly belts through the lift, then feed wheels deliver the cargo into the main shot wheel and backspin contacts. The Limelight gives the drive team a hub reference. Rejection hardware was outside this review.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Concentrating shot geometry in a fixed package leaves space and mass for the telescopes, while chassis yaw and allowable range carry more of the targeting burden. The outer and inner arm pairs occupy separate engagement geometry. During transfer the hanging robot swings and changes the outer hook trajectory. The useful tolerance includes loaded deflection and dynamics at the release from mid, as well as static reach.

subsystems.name: Collector and service joint
subsystems.construction: Early printed hubs with belting flaps. At Chezy a smaller griptape tube, mecanum centering and polycarbonate breakaways with a thicker inner piece.
subsystems.operation: Drops to pick up and feeds directly to the superstructure. Crew swaps breakaways or the complete spare collector.
subsystems.team_rationale: Early flap and Velcro configuration pushed too many balls away. Inner breakaway was thickened because it broke more often.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A deliberate weak joint can protect the downstream frame if the failure load stays above ordinary pickup loads and below the load that bends the frame.
subsystems.interfaces: Roller centering, mounting plates and repeatable handoff to lift.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Team reported swapping the full assembly if breakaway repair would take more than about three minutes. A hard hit can still bend metal plates.
subsystems.unknowns: Actual joint failure load and spare swap procedure.

subsystems.name: Two-ball lift and feedback
subsystems.construction: Custom printed tracking rollers, poly belts, ultrasonic sensing and driver controller haptics.
subsystems.operation: A detected ball advances the lift a set distance. Detecting the next creates room and updates driver feedback.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team describes acquisition notification and limiting held cargo to two.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Distance indexing depends on traction and repeatable sensor placement. Slip can create a mismatch between count and actual stage position.
subsystems.interfaces: Collector exit, first/second cargo spacing and shooter feed nip.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check belt tracking and run a stopped/restarted feed with two worn balls.
subsystems.unknowns: Encoder basis, exact detection location and count recovery logic.

subsystems.name: Fixed launcher
subsystems.construction: Fixed hood and chassis-relative heading, shooter and feed wheels, backspin contacts and Limelight.
subsystems.operation: Shoots from a preferred ring around the hub and farther when needed. Chassis provides azimuth.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team cited weight and serviceability. Field-house testing provided coverage within the fixed geometry.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Removing hood motion trades an alignment degree of freedom for a more limited shot corridor. Route availability is part of measured shooter throughput.
subsystems.interfaces: Lift feed, chassis pose and vision target.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check fixed mount reference and rear-contact wear before retuning distance settings.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact exit angle, range-to-speed map and accuracy distribution.

subsystems.name: Belt telescopes
subsystems.construction: Four continuously belt-routed telescoping arms arranged as inner and outer pairs.
subsystems.operation: Starts from mid. The inner pair catches high and lifts off mid. Chassis swing brings the outer arms to traversal.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team favored belt travel for speed and fewer spring problems, and added two arms to speed the sequence.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Belt timing and hanging dynamics are coupled. A slightly different initial pitch changes the outer hook’s path at the transfer.
subsystems.interfaces: Arm hooks, rung loading, belt travel and chassis swing.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check belt tracking, hook closure and left-right asymmetry. Record missed-transfer recovery as well as clean cycles.
subsystems.unknowns: Rigging, sensors and onseason vs. Chezy timing changes.

revisions: Wilsonville-era flap configuration was followed by rubber, then the Chezy small-tube griptape configuration. The March thread already announced traversal. The later sub-three-second claim belongs to the Chezy discussion.
transferable_principles: Set the sacrificial joint and changeover procedure together. Evaluate fixed-shot geometry against routes, and compare climbs from approach through retained hang.
disconfirming_conditions: The fixed shot loses time when preferred firing lanes are contested. The four-arm speed advantage can reverse if pitch and hook timing require a narrow setup window.
remaining_gaps: Module details, two-ball control states, shot consistency under contact and measured climb distribution by version.

recommended_images.purpose: Seek stills of the Chezy breakaways, collector handoff and telescoping arm pairs.
